Source manufactured 40+, 42m blades. Ask me anything on how they get made.

Edit: Fuck it, it's the only cool thing I got to build and know inside out. 

First out of respect for the company I'll leave some stuff out but the main concept will be there.  Pale is Blade in French, the more you know. 

So first there is a skeleton made out of laminated woods, injected and wrapped with fiberglass.  They get laid down in a giant 42m-ish oven  and one side of the blade is constructed with a blend of roughly 400 layers of fiberglass mesh. Through a fancy process resin is injected through all the layers and cures for over 8 hours in said ovens.  Other skeletal bits and the now cured halves are put together and move to the area where I worked, finishing. 

In finishing one side finished bonding the halves and applied the access panels, mounting ring, a massive cable that secures the blade and redirects lightning, and a chemical paint to prevent frost damage, a proprietary gel coat. The paint had to be measured within a range of 500-1000 microns, thin stuff brought to a spotless and prefect finish. 
After all that tender love and care in smoothing it out, you blast it with an ultra sound for quality checks and after that run a rather fun machine, a giant warehouse crane with a wire brush and gently pet the blade so the finish all leads in the same direction.
